page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.metal-12xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale in-memory computing and data-intensive applications. Driven by a dedicated 48-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor operating at 5.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server provisions one execution thread per physical core without hypervisor overhead. System resources include 1536 GB of system RAM, yielding an expansive 32 GB of memory per core, alongside 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. Hardware-level acceleration features include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and bfloat16 vector extensions, complementing cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional capability across both compute and memory-centric workloads. In synthetic tests, the instance achieves top-tier scores in multi-core stress-ng (201580.87) and Geekbench 6 multi-core (33092.0), driven by its dedicated high-frequency cores. Memory throughput reaches 536.36 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 214.24 GB/sec for large-block writes. In real-world application benchmarks, the server processed 176.61 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 118.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference reflects similar top-tier rankings, attaining 326.28 prompt tokens per second on 7B models and 343.83 generation tokens per second on 135M architectures.

From a cost and resource efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture optimizes compute-per-dollar by eliminating virtualization penalties and maximizing memory bandwidth per core. The integrated 3.8 TB NVMe storage provides high-speed local scratch caching without relying exclusively on remote block devices. However, with an extreme 1:32 core-to-memory ratio and no discrete GPU acceleration, allocating standard compute-bound workloads lacking memory intensity to this instance would represent an inefficient expenditure of provisioned RAM.

This configuration is best suited for enterprise in-memory databases such as Redis, Aerospike, or SAP HANA, large-scale graph databases, distributed big-data caching layers, real-time analytics pipelines, and dense CPU-bound scientific processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.metal-12xl is a high-performance bare-metal instance optimized for memory-dense and enterprise-scale compute tasks. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor at up to 5.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, operating without hypervisor overhead. The system is equipped with 1536 GB of memory, delivering 32 GB of RAM per physical core, integrated with 3800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and 38 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. Architectural support includes AVX-512, BF16, and VAES extensions. Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, delivering 176.61 million Redis SET operations per second and 536.36 GB/sec in large-block read memory bandwidth. Lacking discrete GPUs, it achieves high resource efficiency specifically in memory-bound domains. It is specifically designed for distributed in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, massive caching infrastructures, and intensive scientific modeling.
